messages:
jordan: heads up — after the bmc microcontroller fw push (v2.1.7) to us-west1 racks, r45 has ~30 nodes stuck provisioning. serial consoles are dead and IPMI shows the MCU tripping a powercap; nvram reads as locked. secure-boot bit looks toggled on a few. seeing a lot of GPU nodes drop out of the pool.

kevin: confirmed. started seeing alerts ~08:14 UTC. pgrep on the provisioner shows repeated reboots for those hosts. rolling back the fw on one canary host now (r45-12) to verify.

priya: do we have the bmc rollout job id? pause if it's still active. we should pause the rollout for us-west1 until we understand root cause.

deploy-bot: rollout job id: rollout-2026-03-18-bmc-2.1.7; status: paused by kevin at 08:22 UTC. affected racks: r45 (primary), r46 (partial).

kevin: rollback command used: `bmccli rollback --job rollout-2026-03-18-bmc-2.1.7 --rack r45 --hosts r45-12` — canary reported console back after firmware revert, but nvram still shows locked and one GPU card didn't come back online.

sam_b: note — on previous rollbacks we've seen the MCU cause a brief power inrush that trips the PSU OCP on these older chassis. recommend setting a temporary powercap before mass reboots: `ipmitool raw 0x30 0x70 0x66 0x01 0x00` (sets power cap to 40W) — run on one host first. also run `bmc nvram clear` from the vendor runbook if safe.

jordan: copying the relevant log from r45-12 serial buffer (snipped):
```
[08:13:47] BMC-MCU: powercap event triggered, delta=+1.8A
[08:13:48] BMC-NVRAM: write-protect enabled => lock=1
[08:13:49] IPMI: chassis power state change: forced-off
[08:14:03] KERNEL: gpu0: PCIe device lost link
[08:14:04] PROV: hoststate=provisioning -> error
```

priya: ops-bot graph shows a 15% drop in available gpu capacity in us-west1 during the window. that's ~120 GPUs offline. that's causing queued jobs to backfill into other regions; cost risk increasing for spot/overflow.

ops-bot: alert: gpu_capacity.us-west1 decreased by 15% at 2026-03-18T08:14:00Z. affected services: batch-job-queue, training-preemptible.

kevin: can we drain r45 and r46 gracefully and run the vendor nvram-clear runbook? i'm wary of mass reboots w/o powercap.

sam_b: agree. runbook steps I'm suggesting (one host at a time):
1) set temp powercap (ipmitool raw...)
2) `bmccli revert-firmware --target <host>` and wait for console
3) run `vendor-tool nvram-clear --force` (requires vendor creds)
4) watch for GPU re-enumeration (`lspci | grep -i nvidia`)

jordan: opened an incident: INC-2026-1113 — "oob MCU powercap -> nvram lock -> gpu provisioning failures (us-west1)". toggled paging to oncall-priya. created a jira: INFRA-9812 to track vendor escalation and cost impact.

priya: action items: pause rollout (done), drain r45/r46, run nvram-clear on canary hosts, vendor escalation with logs + BMC dumps, estimate cost exposure and decide on cross-region job redirection. assigning owners: kevin on rollback/runbook, sam_b on powercap/runbook, jordan on incident/jira and cost calc.

kevin: also: don't run mass `bmc update` for the next 48h. we'll need a deeper regression test in staging for MCU changes.

jordan: cost quick estimate: backfill + extra cross-region spot usage + delayed jobs => ~USD 2.6k for the first 3 hours if we keep current backfill. will update with precise numbers.

sam_b: vendor contact pinged (vendor-firmware-bot): ticket VF-4398 created, attaching BMC serial dump and IPMI logs. vendor acknowledged (ETA 4h) to advise if this is fw regression or hardware interaction.

priya: thanks everyone. small ask — capture exact host lists and kernel logs for postmortem. I'll coordinate postmortem doc after incident resolves. :white_check_mark:

kevin: rolling actions now on canary hosts — will report status in thread. :mag:
